author: Andrew

1.said: Short is totally fine. Short right is fine and safe. Left is trouble: big fall-off on the left side of the green. Long is usually dead: chipping back down the hill, green runs back to front. Long-left is super dead.
notes: Green runs back to front. Stay below the hole.
Long-left is the worst miss on the hole.
answers: Straight right of the green: safe (2026-10-01).

2.said: Short hole. Bunker short-left is trouble. Left and long-left: fall-off with bare grass, pretty dead. Right is safe. Short is very safe.
notes: Never left or long. The fall-off left and long-left is bare ground.

3.said: Par 4. Don't drive it super far right: sandy area comes in around 240, blocked out by a tree. Hook it too far left: trees. About 270 from the tee, 25 yds offline left, a tree blocks the view of the green. Go zone is right side or middle of the fairway (bunker short-left of the green). Anything long of the green is super trouble: bare lies, green runs away. Left just over the bunker is okay. Just right of the green, a banked hill collects misses and funnels them to the green. Way right, you're chipping down the slope.
notes: Drive it right-center. Left at 270 is blocked by a tree.
Green runs away from you. Long is dead: bare lies.
The bank just right of the green feeds misses back toward it.

zones.label: Go zone: right-center of the fairway
Right: sandy area, tree blocks the green
Left at 270: tree blocks the view
Just right: bank funnels it back
Way right: chipping down the slope
Long: bare lies, green runs away

answers: Hole plays about 370 from the tee Andrew uses, which is the mapped tee (GPS on 4 rounds: 362-368 to the pin). Card 395 is wrong or from an unused tee, so tee_offset is 0 (2026-10-07).

4.said: Really short, but one of the hardest holes: green runs severely back to front. Short and short-right are good misses. The green runs away from you on the left side, so left is trouble. Anything beyond the green is absolutely dead, especially when greens roll 10-10.5; easy to putt it off the green from above the hole. Stay below the hole at all costs. Spinny green, short club in, so the furthest you'd ever land it is hole high.
notes: Severe back-to-front green. Stay below the hole at all costs.
Land it no further than hole high. Spinny green, short club in.
Fast days (10+): from above the hole you can putt it off the green.

caddy.why: Severe back-to-front slope; above the hole is a likely 3-putt or worse.

5.said: Short par 4. Fairway bunker left where the fairway narrows, about 280 (from the tee). Playground and fence right: out of bounds, can't miss far right off the tee. Long and far left off the tee is a good miss, but trees run along the left side, so don't miss just short on the left. Driver is very rarely the play because the fairway narrows; hit a 235-240 club like a hybrid where it's wider, leaving a full sand wedge. Around the green: short is totally fine, short-right/right side is okay, anything long is absolutely dead (swale behind the green), left is bare lies and the green pitches away.
notes: {plan} off the tee, not driver: the fairway shrinks from 34 yds wide at 200 to 16 at 280.
235–240 off the tee leaves a full sand wedge.
Anything right off the tee is out of bounds (playground fence).
Long is dead: swale behind the green.

caddy.why: Fairway narrows to 16 yds at 280 with a bunker left; OB right. Laying back to ~235 leaves a full wedge.

zones.label: Go zone: lay up to the wide part
Left: trees short of the bunker
Long and far left off the tee
Left: bare lies, green pitches away

answers: OB fence runs all the way along the right side (2026-10-01).

The only left bunker Andrew knows is the fairway bunker at ~280. The map also shows a bunker pin-high left of the green (bunker:1); left unmarked (it sits inside the left 'trouble' zone anyway). Check on the course (2026-10-01).

6.said: Generous drivable par 4, plays about 230; elsewhere it'd be a par 3. I go for it with hybrid and make a lot of birdies. Bunkers along the right side, but short-right off the tee is totally fine and gives a really wide green to hit into: 170-210 off the tee on the right, even 10 yds right of the fairway, is fine. Short is fine off the tee. Left/long-left is dead (trees). Left around the green is not a great place. Beyond the green is dead once you're hitting your approach (green runs away). Off the tee you really want to be short: short-left, short-right.
notes: Go for it: a three-quarter {plan}. Being up near the green makes more birdies than laying back.
If you miss, miss short: short-left and short-right both leave a wide green.
Two bunkers right of the green, at ~220 and ~240 off the tee.
Left and long-left are trees: dead.

options.name: go
options.target: up around the green, short of center; long is dead
options.why: A three-quarter swing allows for a mishit or wind into the face; being up near the green makes more birdies than laying back.

options.name: layup
options.side: right half of the fairway, up to 10 yds right of it

zones.label: Bunker right of the green (~240 off the tee)
Bunker right of the green (~220 off the tee)
zones.note: Not in the map data; placed from Andrew's description. Check on the course.

answers: Two greenside bunkers on the right, ~220 and ~240 off the tee; only the ~240 one is mapped (2026-10-01).
Go club: hybrid at three-quarter speed, for mishits or wind into the face (2026-10-01).

7.said: Another generous par 4. The tee box always gives an uphill lie, which promotes a draw, but a big overhanging tree in the middle of the fairway means you have to cut the ball to reach the green: a mind bender. Off the tee, short of the green is totally fine, short-right fine, right of the green totally fine. Left there's a bunker you don't want to be in. Long of the green: not many people go long off the tee; not great, trouble but not dead. No super dead spot except that left bunker, so I try to leave it short of that.
notes: {plan} off the tee. Usually finishes a little short, which is fine.
The tree ~130 out on the right overhangs the fairway. The uphill tee lie promotes a draw, but you need a cut.
The only real disaster is the bunker left of the green. Leave it short of it.

caddy.why: Tree ~130 out on the right overhangs the fairway; the uphill tee lie promotes a draw.
caddy.aim: short or short-right of the green; never the left bunker

zones.label: Overhanging tree (right side, ~130 off the tee)
zones.note: Tree sits right; its branches overhang the fairway. Placed from Andrew's description.

answers: Tree ~130 off the tee, right side, branches overhang the fairway (2026-10-01).
Andrew doesn't think there's a bunker right of the green; the map shows one pin-high right (bunker:1). Left unmarked; check on the course.

8.said: One of the harder holes: a really long par 3. Short totally fine again. Bunker on the right side isn't very penal because it's short and you have a lot of green to work with. The left side of the hole and the green is tricky. Long is very, very tricky. Same motif as most holes: I tend to club down if I'm in between clubs.
notes: Long par 3: 184 front, 194 center, 204 back. Between clubs, club down. Short is fine.
The bunker short-right isn't penal: lots of green to work with.
Far left is dead: a swale with bald lies leaves a high shot off a bare lie. Long is dead too.

caddy.why: Short is fine; left and long are the trouble.

zones.label: Left side of the hole and green

answers: Far left of the green: dead (swale, bald lies, high shot off a bald lie) (2026-10-01).

9.said: Relatively short par 4. The fairway cants right to left after about 230, so hug the right side. OB fence along the left: you can't go left, you'll be in the parking lot. Lots of eucalyptus trees on the right. Demands a straight ball, not a long one. If I'm driving it well I'll hit driver; I can push it to 50 yds from the green or closer. But a lot of times hybrid off the tee is perfect: it leaves a wedge and is easier to control. Around the green: long and left are pretty dead. Short and short-right are fine. Right there's a fence, so that's kind of dead too. You need to be pretty accurate around the green.
notes: {plan} off the tee leaves a wedge and is easier to control. Driver only when you're driving it well (gets to ~50 out).
The fairway cants right to left past 230. Hug the right side.
OB left: parking-lot fence. Eucalyptus right. A straight ball, not a long one.
Around the green, long, left and right are all dead. Miss short or short-right.
